problems.issue: Median simulated age 46.2 years is implausibly high for predominantly infantile or childhood hepatocerebral MPV17 disease, especially with true hepatic failure in 83% and cirrhosis in 86%. Adult neuropathic presentations exist but do not justify this combination of age and severe hepatic burden.

Hallmark hepatic and metabolic findings are severely underreported: hepatic failure and cirrhosis each appear in only 9%, elevated transaminases in 6–8%, and hypoglycemia in 3%, versus R1-train rates of 33–53%. This teaches a predominantly neuromuscular presentation while hiding the defining hepatocerebral disease.

Examples contain distracting, noncharacteristic findings, particularly bicuspid aortic valve, pectus excavatum, and bulbous nose. Decreased pyruvate dehydrogenase complex activity is also an atypical biochemical emphasis for MPV17-related mtDNA depletion and needs specific support.

summary: The sex balance is plausible, but the adult-heavy age distribution and suppression of hallmark liver disease make these simulated patients clinically misleading.
